clue.text: One better brought up has clenched hand, but he won't use it

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing a word up means reading it from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: to better something is to cap it
one is the Roman numeral I
a clenched hand is a fist

explanation.surface: A man who could top anyone keeps his fist balled up but swears never to throw a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses CAP to PAC. The 'it' of the definition is the clenched hand from the wordplay, so the clue reads almost as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacifist refuses violence, so a man of that belief never uses his fist.

clue.text: Dead and the rest raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means writing it bottom to top

parts.note: et al, Latin for 'and the others', means the rest

explanation.surface: The dead person and everyone else were lifted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses ETAL to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The late So-and-so is a polite way of saying a person who has died.

clue.text: Position for model, a stripper

parts.note: a locus is a position or place
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model can give T

explanation.surface: A spot is found for a model, who is a striptease artist.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a striptease act. In fact a swarm of these insects strips fields bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Locust swarms strip crops and foliage bare, so the insect is cryptically a stripper.

clue.text: Shakespearean reason for purchasing PC?

parts.note: a Thane of Fife from Macbeth, whose name split in two says an Apple computer is broken, which would be a good reason to buy a PC instead

explanation.definitionFit: Macduff, the Thane of Fife who kills Macbeth, is a Shakespearean character whose name splits as Mac + duff.

clue.text: A South American country admits addict ultimately on crack

indicators.note: a country admitting something lets it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Peru is a country in South America

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word addict

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A South American nation is said to let in drug users who end up hooked on crack cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' puts T, the last letter of addict (picked by 'ultimately'), inside PERU.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is an opening, and a crack is a narrow opening, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: One doing for the done for?

definitions.text: One doing for the done for?

parts.words: One doing for the done for?
parts.note: to do for someone is to look after them, and someone done for is dead, so this is a person who takes care of the dead

explanation.definitionFit: An undertaker arranges funerals, looking after people who have died.

clue.text: Flower in trouble had to be pulled up

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling words up turns the run of letters backwards

parts.note: to ail is to be in trouble or unwell
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flower in poor condition had to be uprooted from the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be pulled up' turns the whole run AILHAD backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a garden flower with bright, many-petalled blooms.

clue.text: Spain so regularly occupies its wine lover

indicators.note: one thing occupying another is sitting inside it, so these letters go within the wine

parts.note: cava is a Spanish sparkling wine

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words Spain so, starting from the first

explanation.surface: Spain is often taken up with its own wine, and with someone who loves it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' is a link that ties the wine to Spain in the surface; cava is the Spanish counterpart of champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova was the famous Venetian seducer, so his name is used for any great lover.

clue.text: Secretary's individual letters, one in black and white?

parts.note: a secretary is a PA (personal assistant), whose letters are P and A
saying the letters individually spells them out one by one with 'and' between
the second letter of PA, the secretary's abbreviation

explanation.surface: A secretary spells out her letters, one in black ink on white paper.
explanation.walkthrough: PA spelt out letter by letter is 'P and A'. The black and white surface suggests print, but it is the animal's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda has black and white fur.

clue.text: Flier in park I tested

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the run of words park I tested

explanation.surface: I tried out a flying toy in the park.
explanation.definitionFit: A kite is a toy that flies, and also a bird of prey, so it is a flier either way.

clue.text: Soft body part blender processed in month, decapitated

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed in the cut-down month
a decapitated word loses its head, i.e. its first letter

parts.note: July is a month of the year

indicators.note: food processed in a blender is mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soft cut of meat goes into the blender in the month the cook lost their head.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen surface makes 'Soft body part' read like a cut of meat; 'month, decapitated' needs the month that suits the letters, and only July fits.
explanation.definitionFit: The underbelly is the soft underside of an animal's body.

clue.text: Devil beset by hindrance, a sucker

indicators.note: a piece beset by another is surrounded by it, so it goes inside

parts.note: a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'
an imp is a little devil

explanation.surface: A demon held back by some obstacle turns out to be a gullible fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a gullible person. In fact the definition is a shellfish that clings to rocks by suction.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet is a shellfish that clings to rocks by suction, so it is a sucker.

clue.text: Dud, Dud, Neil, Rod and Pam

indicators.note: something dud is faulty or broken, so the names that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of friends' names: Dud twice, then Neil, Rod and Pam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dud' (the second one) rearranges NEIL ROD PAM. The first 'Dud' is an example of the answer. Pam, Neil and Rod are all reversible too, as MAP, LIEN and DOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The word dud spells the same forwards and backwards, so it is an example of such a word.

clue.text: Tropical creature a bit unfortunate to be swallowed by backward sod

indicators.note: one piece swallowed by another goes inside it
backward tells us to read the word for sod in reverse order

parts.note: sod is turf, a piece of grass with its roots

indicators.note: something unfortunate has gone wrong, so the letters of a bit are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unlucky tropical animal ends up gulped down by a piece of turf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tropical creature' points at the whole answer; 'sod' is the grassy kind, not the insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit bats are tropical flying mammals that feed on fruit.

clue.text: One who designs a register of homes in Swine Avenue?

indicators.note: a list of something has that something placed before it in the answer

parts.note: pigs (swine) live in sties, so their homes are each a sty
a register is a list

explanation.surface: A designer draws up a directory of houses on Pig Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swine Avenue' is an invented street for pigs, whose homes are sties.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylist designs clothes, hair or looks, so a stylist is one who designs.

clue.text: Crack cocaine's heading into US city, providing financial stability

parts.note: to crack a puzzle is to solve it

indicators.note: into puts the initial letter of cocaine inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: NY is short for New York, the US city

indicators.note: a word's heading is its first letter

explanation.surface: Crack cocaine making its way into an American city brings its dealers a steady income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like the drug but means to work out. 'heading' takes C from cocaine, and 'into' puts it inside NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Solvency is the state of being able to pay your debts, which is financial stability.

clue.text: Newspaper seller provides signal for radio operator

parts.note: a beck is a beckoning gesture, a signal, as in 'at one's beck and call'
a ham is an amateur radio operator

explanation.surface: A newsagent sends a signal over the airwaves to a radio enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: David Beckham, the England footballer, was so famous that a picture of him on the front page helped sell newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity whose face on the front page boosts sales could be called a seller of newspapers.

clue.text: Means to declare for a month of Sundays

parts.note: to aver is to declare firmly
a month of Sundays is a very long time, i.e. ages

explanation.surface: Ways of saying something forever.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics a mean is an average, so means are averages.

clue.text: Cuba and Carthage, virtually riotous, had problems rowing

indicators.note: riotous suggests wild disorder, so the letters are rearranged
virtually means almost entirely, so the last letter of Carthage is dropped

explanation.surface: Two places, Cuba and ancient Carthage, are close to rioting and find themselves in a squabble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' cuts CARTHAGE to CARTHAG, and 'riotous' rearranges CUBA with it. 'rowing' looks like quarrelling but means using oars.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a crab is a rowing term for fouling a stroke, when the oar jams in the water.

clue.text: Head of government given refusal to enter country, a bloomer

indicators.note: to enter a place is to go inside it, so these letters go inside the country

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A leader is refused entry to a nation, which is a real blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is British slang for a blunder, which the surface plays on, but here it is a flowering tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnolia is a tree with large showy flowers, so it is a thing that blooms.

clue.text: Commercial weakness elicits recommendation

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an ad
a vice is a moral weakness

explanation.surface: A failing in the advertising world brings a word of warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is guidance on what to do, so it is a recommendation.

clue.text: 19 9 in the East End?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held is '19 9 in the East End? (6)'. Neither 19 (CAUGHT A CRAB) nor 9 (PANDA) in this grid, nor any search, explains how they lead to BURGER, so the cross-reference cannot be parsed.

clue.text: Object of ridicule on disc

parts.note: the butt of a joke is the object of ridicule

explanation.surface: Someone is laughed at for appearing on a record.
explanation.definitionFit: A button is a small disc sewn onto clothing.

clue.text: Cox's position keeping west, why boat might sink?

indicators.note: one piece keeping another holds it inside

parts.note: the cox of a rowing eight sits facing the eight oarsmen and directs them, so is in a position over eight

explanation.surface: A coxswain stays to the west, wondering why the rowing boat is going down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a rowing eight the cox is in charge of the eight rowers, so is placed 'over eight'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat carrying too much weight would sink, so being too heavy explains it.

clue.text: See 19
Sound punishment for murderer

indicators.note: sound means we hear the word for punishment said out loud

parts.note: the cane is a punishment, a beating with a stick

explanation.surface: A good beating is the right punishment for a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning proper, but it signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Cain killed his brother Abel and became the first murderer.

clue.text: Funny issue of clown losing rear end touring motorway

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the cut-down clown goes around the motorway
a word losing its rear end drops its last letter

parts.note: Coco was a famous circus clown
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A clown loses the seat of his trousers on a trip up the motorway and puts out a funny publication.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco was a well-known British circus clown, and the M1 is Britain's main motorway from London north to Leeds, written with the figure read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic is a magazine of cartoon strips, so each funny edition is one issue.

clue.text: Unreliable person to send anything back

indicators.note: back says the whole run of letters is to be read backwards

parts.note: to remit money is to send it
owt is northern English dialect for anything

explanation.surface: An untrustworthy type is asked to return whatever was posted.
explanation.walkthrough: OWT is Yorkshire dialect for 'anything'. 'back' turns REMITOWT backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-timer is unfaithful, secretly seeing two partners, so is an unreliable person.
